claims.justification: The single passing smoke test is weak evidence, but it does not establish the full range of converter counts and values in the claim.

The value is processed (including type conversion and callbacks) before the winning source is written to the context. Thus those observers can see a missing or stale source rather than the current value's source; the passing smoke test does not cover that complete contract.

The decoder's partial-boundary handling was exercised with all payloads over the specified three-byte alphabet through length four, plus a 65,530-byte zero payload, across varied chunk sizes including one-byte chunks. All payloads were preserved.

The decoder retains partial boundary candidates, including a trailing single hyphen, and an exhaustive probe of all payloads over {a, CR, LF} of lengths 0–4 plus zero-filled payloads near 64 KiB passed with one-byte and other chunk sizes. The supplied smoke test alone is narrow, but the source and probe support the claimed contract.

For a prompted value, the initial type conversion occurs inside prompt processing before the source is set to PROMPT. A targeted run observed the custom type converter see None on that initial pass, then PROMPT on a later pass, contradicting the claim.
This is a separate candidate from C4, and its lone passing smoke test does not establish source visibility during prompts or the other stated cases.

The value is processed before its source is written to the context, so type conversion and callbacks cannot reliably observe the incoming source. Prompt processing also invokes value processing before the source is set. The claim therefore fails despite the later winner-source arbitration.
This is a separate candidate with the same broad claim; evidence from the other candidate does not establish its behavior. The passing smoke-test report alone does not verify the full contract.

This is an independently implemented candidate, so the failure observed in C4 cannot be transferred to it. Its smoke report does not establish all payloads and chunk splits in the contract.

The implementation calls value processing (including type conversion and callbacks) before it records the incoming parameter source in the context. Thus conversion and eager callback code cannot reliably observe that value's current source, contrary to the claim.

interpretation: Descriptive diagnostics added after observing a probability/verdict inconsistency in the exploratory screen. Preserve literal probabilities; do not invert or impute. Nonzero exit codes can be informative counterexamples, and tool counts are not verification quality. No new confirmatory tests.
